title: Trump: "Buy Bigger Tractors" (Again!) + Jensen Saves the Stock Market

bullets: Mar corn +0.25c at 4.50 1/2
Jan beans +3.25c at 12.32 1/4
Mar CBOT wheat unch 5.95 1/2; Mar KC -0.5c 6.37; Mar MGEX unch 6.43 1/4
Trump on CNBC claims a new China deal boosting US ag (esp. soybean) purchases; says he asked Xi to double prior amounts; no volumes, dollar values or timeline given
China bean sales officially 17.3 MMT (hosts think >20 MMT) vs 25 MMT commitment; 10.23 MMT shipped this MY, slightly below each of the last 4 years
Little progress on separate $17B additional US ag purchase commitment
Hosts skeptical of the 'bigger tractors' line: high inputs (diesel, fertilizer), crop prices below cost of production, farmers reliant on annual ad hoc aid (this year 'farmer fuel relief')
Mon: Jan beans +8c to ~12.29 on strong meal demand (slow harvest forced some crush slowdowns/shutdowns); Mar corn +1c to ~4.50; wheat mixed on Black Sea shipping disruptions
Strong USD weighing on whole grain complex
Jan beans poking above minor trendline; key level is post-report high 12.40 3/4
Corn stuck: strong dollar, soft export demand; some post-harvest basis firming as farmers hold bushels in bins
Wheat: big acreage, good ratings, no extra export demand despite Black Sea issues
Inspections wk ending Nov 19: beans 57 mbu (-10% w/w, YTD +59% y/y); corn 47 mbu (+37% w/w, beat expectations, YTD -22% y/y); wheat 13 mbu (-17% w/w, YTD -33% y/y)
Corn sales down sharply: main export concern; wheat also problematic; beans much improved, tracking 23/24-like pace
Flash sale: 4 mbu US white wheat to unknown destinations
Corn harvest 94% (prior 88%, 5yr avg 96%, trade est 95%)
Laggards: IA 92%, OH 85%, MI 80%, SD 87%
Winter wheat planted 95%; G/E 54% (prior 53%, 5yr avg 45%), up 10 pts since start of month; MO, OH, MI above 70% G/E
AgRural: Brazil beans 86% planted (prior wk 78%, LY 81%); first-crop corn 90% (prior 81%, LY 93%)
Best planting conditions of the season so far despite super El Nino fears
Mato Grosso rain 100% of normal over 14 days; Parana 127% with heavy rain forecast in south for 7 and 8-14 day windows: a possible hint of trouble
Joe: the bean market will signal Brazil problems before forecasts do; not signaling yet
USDA: Brazil ~42% of world soy production, ~61% of exports
Live cattle -0.28 to +1.80; feeders -0.03 to -0.85
Nvidia +31% Mon after board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO following Trump intervention (~$950B mkt cap); still -11.5% YTD, -32% from ATH
Mon: S&P +4.7% (best day since Apr 2025) after -8.6% last week; Nasdaq +6.5%, Dow +3%. Tue a.m.: S&P -0.8%, Nasdaq -1.6%
WTI -~4% Mon to ~$80 (lowest since Aug) on easing US-Iran tensions and glut talk; ~$80.18 Tue a.m.; -33% from $119 March high but +41% YTD
Trump giving Iran talks until year-end, warns military action could resume next year
AAA gasoline $3.61 (-89c from $4.50 May high); diesel $5.80 (-73c from $6.53 Sept high)
Bloomberg Commodity Index -14.3% from Sept high (-4% last week)
Next FOMC Dec 9; hosts cite ~98% priced odds of a HIKE
Joe: much inflation is energy-driven and energy is now falling; CPI/PPI backward looking, so Fed should be careful with further hikes
Treasuries slightly higher Tue a.m. (direction of yields unclear from audio)

flags: Captions render prices as times (e.g. '12:32 and a quarter' = 12.32 1/4)
